Youth Apostles — youthapostles.org — HIT. Per-person pages at youthapostles.org/<firstnamelastname> (no hyphen, no /missionaries/ prefix): /tylerfabian, /josephfrommelt, /jimharbour, /nickeastman, /gabrielchurchill, /nickzaso, /austinmee. Titles are 'First Last | Youth Apostles'. Roster hub at /missionaries, program page /missionaryprogram, office staff roster /officestaff. Small org (Diocese of Arlington origin, ministering in several states); the flat-slug shape means site: queries surface person pages only a few at a time and -surname exclusions were ignored by the engine, so the roster is probably not exhausted. A fetch-enabled pass on https://www.youthapostles.org/missionaries and /officestaff would close it cheaply.

Vagabond Missions — vagabondmissions.com — MISS as a per-person surface. Roster page https://vagabondmissions.com/meet-our-missionaries/ is live and the team page /team/ lists staff with 'Support <Name>' buttons, but no per-person URL is indexed: everything surfaced is a city landing page (/pittsburgh, /okc, /baton-rouge, /wichita, /philadelphia, /steubenville, /oklahoma-city) or a generic /support and /support-our-mission/. Names do not appear in snippets, so the roster is rendered client-side or as image cards and the 'Support' links almost certainly point off-domain to a payment processor. Nine sites: Baton Rouge LA, Greenville NC, Indianapolis IN, Mobile AL, Oklahoma City OK, Philadelphia PA, Pittsburgh PA, Steubenville OH, Wichita KS. Record the roster URL for a future fetch-enabled wave — this is the best remaining unopened Catholic roster.

Christ in the City — christinthecity.org — MISS by deliberate anonymization. The shape is right (/missionary/<slug>, plus city rosters /denver-missionaries/ and /philadelphia-missionaries/ and a hub /missionary/) but the slugs are first-name-plus-initial: https://christinthecity.org/missionary/grace-s/. Under the hard rules that is unemittable, and the withheld surname looks intentional for a young-adult household ministry serving the homeless. Do not re-probe for names; a fetch would not help because the surnames are not published.

Catholic Christian Outreach (Canada) — cco.ca — MISS, but the closest near-hit after Youth Apostles. CCO states plainly that missionaries fund their own salary via 'Support Team Partnership Development', and the roster at https://cco.ca/our-missionaries/ is organized by region (Atlantic, Central, Pacific, Western) plus HQ staff, with instructions to 'join a missionary support team by clicking on their picture'. But no per-person URL is indexed under cco.ca and no missionary names appear in any snippet — the picture grid is client-side and the click target is likely a give.cco.ca form (which per the brief's table is NOT a hit anyway). Note: this is the Canadian Catholic CCO, distinct from the already-worked Coalition for Christian Outreach. Worth one fetch-enabled pass on the roster URL.

The Culture Project — thecultureproject.org — MISS. Support-raising missionary model is real (13-month commitments, recent college grads) but the site has a single shared /about/staff/ page and no per-person path; the rest of the namespace is /apply/, /schedule/, /plan/ and WordPress tag archives (/tag/missionary/). No names in snippets.

The Evangelical Catholic — evangelicalcatholic.org — MISS. Surface is /faq/, /lifegroups/, /donate/ only. It is a parish-training organization that trains OTHER agencies' missionaries rather than fielding its own support-raised roster. No staff or missionary directory surfaced.

Miles Christi — mileschristi.org — MISS, nothing indexed at all on a site:-scoped probe. A religious order (priests and brothers under vows, not personally support-raised staff), so likely a poor archetype fit regardless.

FrassatiUSA — frassatiusa.org — MISS for this project though the URL shape teases. It does serve per-person pages at /people/<first-last> (e.g. /people/father-charles-mangano), but the organization promotes the spirituality of Bl. Pier Giorgio Frassati; /donations is a single general appeal and the /people/ entries are clergy and family figures associated with the cause, not support-raising missionaries. Do not mine.

Camp Veritas (campveritas.com), Totus Tuus (totustuusteachers.org), Mission of the Redeemer (missionoftheredeemer.com) — MISS. A combined site:-scoped probe returned zero results from all three domains. Either not indexed, or the domains I guessed are wrong: Totus Tuus in particular is a diocesan summer-catechesis program run separately by each diocese rather than one national agency, so there is no single roster to mine and its teachers are seasonal, diocese-paid, and not personal-support-raised.

Corpus Christi — no national apostolate domain found. The probe surfaced only 'Corpus Christi Outreach Ministries', a Blogspot site (corpuschristioutreachministries.blogspot.com), which is a personal devotional blog and not a sending agency. Treat the brief's 'Corpus Christi' entry as unresolvable without a specific domain.

St. Paul Street Evangelization — stpaulstreetevangelization.com — MISS. No indexed roster or per-person page; the only team surface found was a Facebook group for team leaders and regional coordinators. Volunteer street-evangelization teams rather than salaried support-raised missionaries, so a weak archetype fit.

Apostolate for Family Consecration — afc.org — NOT PROBED, but noted from an incidental result: afc.org/support-a-missionary/ is a pooled appeal covering youth missionaries' food, housing and clothing, i.e. a fund page, not a per-person page. Low priority for a future wave.

needs_review.issue: Named on the Youth Apostles site but no citable page of their own
needs_review.finding: Eric McDade, described in a snippet as a Youth Apostles full member and seminarian for the Diocese of Arlington.
needs_review.evidence: Surfaced in the summary of a site:youthapostles.org query alongside https://www.youthapostles.org/campusministry; I could not confirm which page actually names him and no /ericmcdade page appeared.
needs_review.recommendation: Fetch https://www.youthapostles.org/campusministry and test https://www.youthapostles.org/ericmcdade. Also confirm whether Youth Apostles seminarians raise personal support — the community appears to fund them centrally, which would make him Tier B or out of scope entirely.

needs_review.issue: Seminarian funded by the community rather than by personal support
needs_review.finding: Peter Clem, Youth Apostles seminarian, fourth year of theology at Mount St. Mary's Seminary, Emmitsburg MD.
needs_review.evidence: Snippet from a site:youthapostles.org query states the community bears a $35,000/year cost per seminarian; the appeal appears to sit on https://www.youthapostles.org/cornerstone, a campaign page, not a personal page.
needs_review.recommendation: Do not emit as Tier A. If a per-person page exists he is a Tier B staff_directory record at best; the cost-per-seminarian framing points to a pooled fund, which the brief classes as not a hit.

needs_review.issue: Full name known but only a blog author-archive URL
needs_review.finding: John Lilly, author of multiple Youth Apostles blog posts.
needs_review.evidence: https://www.youthapostles.org/author/jlilly/page/2 — WordPress author archive; slug is first-initial+surname, title gives the full name.
needs_review.recommendation: An author archive is not a page about the person and carries no support ask. Check whether https://www.youthapostles.org/johnlilly exists before creating a record; his role and support status are unknown.

needs_review.issue: Name appears only as a content tag
needs_review.finding: Tiffany Lambert, associated with Youth Apostles content.
needs_review.evidence: https://www.youthapostles.org/tag/tiffany-lambert — a tag archive, not a profile.
needs_review.recommendation: Determine whether she is Youth Apostles staff, a Women Youth Apostles member, or an outside contributor before any record is made. Women Youth Apostles is a separate sister community (womenyouthapostles.org) that was not probed this wave and is a strong candidate for the next one.

needs_review.issue: Ministry publishes missionaries under first name plus initial
needs_review.finding: Christ in the City publishes its entire missionary roster without surnames, e.g. /missionary/grace-s/.
needs_review.recommendation: Record as a permanent negative for name-level enumeration. The surnames are withheld on the ministry's own pages for young adults doing street ministry with the homeless; do not attempt to recover them from other sources.
